title: Xanthe and the Visitor
premise: Dominic Winterbourne returns to Winterbourne House to bury her twin brother Ambrose, only to learn the body in the casket is wearing her face. The house she inherited was built by founders who sealed something beneath the old well, and every mirror on the property now lags a single second behind reality—long enough for Dominic to glimpse what moves when she doesn't. As the well begins to refill, the lag widens, and the reflected version of Dominic grows bolder, claiming it is the real twin and that Ambrose's death was its escape. To survive, Dominic must complete the founders' interrupted ritual before the water rises, choosing between erasing herself entirely or binding her reflection forever—and in the end she seals the well by taking her reflection's place, letting the other walk out into the world wearing her name.
about_author: Elodie Vasquez is a former funeral home archivist from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing estate inventories of houses no one wanted to inherit. Her fiction draws on the quiet dread of family property, and 'Xanthe and the Visitor' is her third novel.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Casket
chapters.summary: Dominic arrives at Winterbourne House for Ambrose's funeral and finds the corpse wearing her own features, down to the childhood scar. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief curdling into denial as she convinces herself it's embalming error or cruel mistake.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Reasonable Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Dominic and Ambrose hear noises beneath the floorboards; their mother teaches them to name the sounds until they sound ordinary. POV: Dominic (past). Emotional beat: the origin of her survival strategy—invisibility through rationalization.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Haunted Estate
chapters.summary: Dominic catalogs the house per the will's terms and finds the founders' ledger describing a ritual 'finished at the well'—with the final pages torn out. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity; the first crack in her explanations.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: The hallway mirror reflects Dominic lifting her cup a beat after she does. She tests every mirror in the house; all lag exactly one second. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold vertigo—the moment explanation fails.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Kept Count
chapters.summary: Elderly neighbor Maren Cole reveals the founders sealed something in the well in 1893 and that every Winterbourne heir has 'kept the count' of seconds. POV: Dominic with Maren scene. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—Maren begs her to leave before the count reaches sixty.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Room, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Dominic finds Ambrose's bedroom preserved, his journal detailing how he fed the reflection small truths about himself to keep it docile—and how he stopped. POV: Dominic reading. Emotional beat: guilt; she realizes her invisibility made her brother the target.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: At the covered well, the boards pulse like a heartbeat. The mirror-lag stretches to two seconds. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: dread deepening into compulsion—the house wants her at the well.

chapters.title: The Visitor Introduces Itself
chapters.summary: In the great hall mirror, the reflection speaks first, calling itself Xanthe—the name struck from the founders' ledger. It claims to be the buried twin of the first Winterbourne. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: terror mixed with terrible recognition.

chapters.title: Loyalty of the Living
chapters.summary: Dominic tries to burn the mirrors; the fire refuses them. Maren arrives to help and sees Xanthe wear Dominic's face mid-conversation. POV: alternating Dominic/Maren. Emotional beat: Maren's loyalty fractures—she flees, and Dominic is truly alone.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Searching the chapel crypt, Dominic finds the missing ledger pages sewn into Ambrose's burial suit lining: the ritual requires a willing twin's consent. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: horrified understanding of why Ambrose died.

chapters.title: Three Seconds
chapters.summary: The lag hits three seconds; reflections now show rooms as they were decades ago. Dominic watches her mother's suicide play out in glass. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: grief weaponized—Xanthe offers to bring Ambrose back if Dominic consents.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Landing
chapters.summary: At the stairwell mirror, Xanthe negotiates: consent to swap places, and Ambrose lives again in memory and flesh. Dominic nearly agrees. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme at full pressure.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren returns, confessing she was the one who told young Ambrose about the well; her family were the founders' servants. She brings the iron counterweight used in 1893. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: inherited guilt meeting inherited duty.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Water rises through the floors; the house floods ankle-deep with mirror-still water that shows Xanthe walking beside Dominic everywhere. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: siege mentality—the house itself has chosen sides.

chapters.title: Reading the Founders' Hands
chapters.summary: Deciphering marginalia, Dominic learns the 1893 ritual failed because the founder's twin refused consent—and was drowned instead, becoming Xanthe. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: rage at the inheritance; truth over family myth.

chapters.title: Sixty Seconds
chapters.summary: The lag reaches a full minute. Dominic lives a minute behind her own reflection, watching Xanthe rehearse her life. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: identity dissolution—who is original after twenty years of hiding?

chapters.title: The Consent Clause
chapters.summary: Dominic discovers consent can be given falsely: the ritual binds whoever believes themselves agreed. She begins performing willingness while preparing the counterweight. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Night of Standing Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe steps fully out of the flooded hall mirror; the sisters confront each other across rising water, each claiming the name Dominic. POV: both. Emotional beat: climax of identity—two claimants, one life.

chapters.title: The Ritual at the Well
chapters.summary: At the open well, Dominic speaks the founders' words, offering false consent; Xanthe seizes her anyway, and both fall toward the water as the counterweight drops. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, betrayal, and split-second choice.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: Submerged, Dominic meets the drowned founder's twin and understands the seal requires a willing keeper, not a prisoner. She chooses to stay—not as victim but as warden. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed in surrender.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Walks Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe, now believing herself Dominic, buries 'Ambrose' properly and sells the house to Maren's grandchildren. Mirrors everywhere run perfectly on time. POV: Xanthe-as-Dominic. Emotional beat: eerie peace built on stolen identity.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Count
chapters.summary: Epilogue: beneath the still water, Dominic keeps the count, and occasionally a mirror somewhere lags one second—for a stranger, a warning. The last line reveals she counts not seconds but visitors. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: haunting resolution—truth kept, loyalty transformed into vigil.
